root_causes: Lack of task-directed actions: the agents repeatedly executed Wait and generic Explore without ever issuing necessary manipulation actions (navigate-to-counter, pickup kettle/potato, navigate-to-stool, place-on-stool).
No progression in high-level planning: the planning step remained at 1 throughout, indicating the planner did not update subgoals or generate a concrete action sequence after initial exploration.

Ineffective exploration policy: Agent 1’s Explore[kitchen_1] calls caused only small pose changes near (−0.33, 13.71) and did not move the agent toward the known object locations at (1.23, 12.25) and (2.55, 12.04).

Underutilization of known state: despite the environment state clearly reporting the positions of the kettle and potato on counter_34, the controller did not exploit this information to trigger navigation and pickup.
Single-role agent behavior: Agent 0 remained idle (continuous Wait) and did not participate in task execution, missing an opportunity for parallelization (e.g., one agent per object).
improvement_suggestions: Introduce a goal-conditioned action policy that, once task objects and receptacles are localized, switches from generic Explore/Wait to explicit navigate–pickup–navigate–place primitives targeting those entities.

Add a planning-state progression mechanism: upon confirming the location of kettle_0 and potato_1, advance the planner from exploration to manipulation subgoals and enforce timeouts on unproductive exploration loops.

Implement exploration termination and re-planning: detect repeated state patterns (same positions, same observations) over N steps and trigger a re-plan that explicitly routes the agent to the objects’ coordinates.
Leverage object position feedback: use the reported (x, y, z) of kettle_0 and potato_1 to compute navigation targets (e.g., waypoints near counter_34) instead of relying on unguided Explore actions.

Activate both agents with complementary roles: assign Agent 0 to retrieve one object and Agent 1 the other, or have one agent scout and the other execute manipulation, avoiding prolonged idle Wait for Agent 0.
Introduce simple success-check heuristics per subgoal (e.g., ‘am I holding kettle_0?’, ‘is kettle_0 on a stool?’) and abort or adjust behavior when these remain false for many steps.
Incorporate a high-level finite-state machine (explore → approach counter → pick up object → approach stool → place object) to prevent the system from remaining in the exploration state indefinitely.
overall_assessment: The execution failed completely to address the task, with agents stuck in an exploration/wait loop and never attempting to pick up or move the kettle or potato despite knowing their locations. Overall coordination, planning progression, and task-directed action selection were very poor.
task_instruction: Move the kettle and potato from the counter to the stool in the kitchen.
